notes: The wording says that Nebuchadnezzar bound Jehoiakim to take him to Babylon; this sentence does not explicitly say that the journey took place.
The Hebrew word translated “palace” can also mean a temple.
The pinned Hebrew text says “eight.” Second Kings 24:8 says “eighteen.” The difference is retained.
The Hebrew calls Zedekiah Jehoiachin’s “brother” here. Second Kings 24:17 identifies him as Jehoiachin’s uncle.
“Again and again” represents an idiom of rising early and sending, emphasizing persistent effort.
The land’s rest recalls Leviticus 26:34–35. Jeremiah 25:11–12 and 29:10 speak of seventy years. The verse joins these themes without explaining a detailed chronology.
Ezra 1:1–3 repeats much of this proclamation, with some differences in wording. Chronicles ends with the invitation to go up.
vocabulary: A large unit of weight used for precious metals.
The center of thought, intention, and resolve as well as feeling.
A name used here for the Babylonian forces.
Periods of rest; here the desolate land itself is pictured resting.
